Convert this Playwright boilerplate into a real, client-specific project. The repo ships with placeholders (`playwright-boilerplate`, `https://your-url-here.com`, `example.com`, OneTrust consent, `frontend-playwright` Testmo source, partly-stale docs); your job is to replace them with this client's real values.

This is a **one-time, repo-wide change** — interview me first, show a plan, get my go-ahead, _then_ edit. Once the placeholders are gone there's no clean undo short of git.

**Before you start:** read `/AGENTS.md`, then the files you'll touch (`package.json`, `config/dev.ts`, `utils/environmentManager.ts`, `testFixtures/base.ts`, `types/envConfig.ts`, `config/projects.ts`, and — if the client has logins — `objects/pages/LoginPage.ts`, `tests/auth.setup.ts`, `utils/auth.ts`). Also read the companion map **`onboard-client-project.references.md`** (same folder) — it's the exact file-by-file list of every placeholder, with templates for env files, consent providers, auth, and CI tokens. Keep it open while you work. Finally, check `git status`: if the tree is dirty, suggest I commit/stash first so the onboarding diff is reviewable on its own.

## Interview me

Ask about each area below in order. Skip an area only if the user has already provided that information earlier in the conversation, or explicitly says they want to skip it. Then summarise the plan — which files change, what gets deleted — and wait for my go-ahead.

1. **Project identity** — client/project name (→ `package.json` `name`, kebab-case), description, author/team. If the name is not already kebab-case, show the proposed conversion (e.g. "Acme Corp" → "acme-corp") and ask the user to confirm before writing it to `package.json`.
2. **Application & environments** — which environments exist (`dev`/`qa`/`staging`/`prod`/…) and the base URL for each. Also ask whether the suite needs to cover more than one site/brand/domain under the same environments (e.g. a UK site and a US site). If so, stop this step and hand off to the **`add-multi-site-support`** skill (`.github/skills/add-multi-site-support/SKILL.md`) instead of scaffolding one `config/<env>.ts` per brand — it restructures config/fixtures/the project matrix for that dimension properly; wiring it ad hoc here gets unmaintainable fast. Otherwise, for a single site, ask whether to scaffold a `config/<env>.ts` for each env now, or only add a comment block listing the planned envs at the top of `utils/environmentManager.ts` for later. If the user chooses to defer, write the list as a TODO comment in that file and nothing else. For each env wired, create `config/<env>.ts` and register it in `utils/environmentManager.ts`. Also check which `config/*.ts` env files already exist in the boilerplate. Delete any that are not in the client's confirmed env list, following the same deletion procedure described for `dev`. **If there's no `dev` env, delete `config/dev.ts`, drop it from the manager map, and change the default fallback `process.env.ENV || 'dev'`** to the new default — a `|| 'dev'` pointing at a deleted config throws at runtime. Also ask about the optional SEO bits (`xmlSitemapUrl`, `robotsTxt`, `searchUrl`, `articleUrl`); drop keys that don't apply — **but first grep kept specs/objects for `getValue('<key>')`** (e.g. `tests/globalSeo.spec.ts` reads `robotsTxt`) and fix the dependents, or `pnpm typecheck` fails. Update `.env.example` to match.
3. **Consent & analytics** — which cookie-consent provider (the boilerplate pre-seeds OneTrust's `OptanonAlertBoxClosed` in `testFixtures/base.ts`; swap the cookie name — see the references table for Cookiebot/Civic/Osano/TrustArc; if no banner, make the fixture a no-op). And any extra analytics/tag hosts to add to the `ANALYTICS_HOSTS` regex beyond GTM/GA.
4. **Authentication** — does the app have logins/authenticated tests? The boilerplate ships a dormant, provider-agnostic auth scaffold (`objects/pages/LoginPage.ts` template, `tests/auth.setup.ts` setup project, `primaryUserTest`/`secondaryUserTest` fixtures, gated by `isAuthConfigured()` in `utils/auth.ts`). Ask:
   - **No auth?** Delete `objects/pages/LoginPage.ts`, `tests/auth.setup.ts`, `tests/authExample.spec.ts`, the `loginPage` entries in `types/types.ts` + `testFixtures/base.ts`, the `primaryUserTest`/`secondaryUserTest` exports, the `setup` project block in `playwright.config.ts`, `utils/auth.ts`, and the auth keys in `types/envConfig.ts` (`EnvConfig`) + `config/*.ts`. Confirm before deleting.
   - **Has auth?** Gather: the **identity provider** (Okta, Auth0, Azure AD B2C, bespoke form…) and **login URL**; the **role names** (boilerplate ships `primaryUser`/`secondaryUser` — rename across `authFiles`, the setup tests, the fixtures, and `.auth/*.json` paths if the client prefers e.g. `member`/`admin`); and **credentials** for each role. Then rewrite `LoginPage.ts`'s `← TODO` locators and `login()` steps for the real provider (use the Playwright MCP browser to find stable locators; for SSO-redirect flows uncomment the variant in `login()`). Set `loginUrl` and the per-role creds in `config/<env>.ts`.
   - **Credentials — config vs `.env`:** they default to `config/<env>.ts`. **Ask whether to keep them there or move secrets to `.env`** (real passwords shouldn't be committed). If `.env`: uncomment the `*_USER_EMAIL`/`*_USER_PASSWORD` vars in `.env.example`, have the client populate their own `.env`, and change the config values to read `process.env.PRIMARY_USER_EMAIL` etc.
   - **Which projects run authenticated tests?** All projects depend on `setup`; if only some browsers should run `@authenticated` specs, add `grepInvert: [/@authenticated/]` to the others in `config/projects.ts` (the source pattern ran member tests on Chrome only). Confirm whether one auth role is enough — if so, drop `secondaryUser` everywhere; if they need a third, add an `authFiles` entry + setup test + fixture.
5. **Browser matrix** — which of `config/projects.ts`'s projects the client needs; trim the rest, or keep all. If you trim, make sure CI's `--project Chrome "Mobile Chrome"` references still resolve, and that any `@authenticated` `grepInvert` rules still target the projects you intend.
6. **CI/CD** — confirm Azure DevOps + Testmo. Gather `workingDir` (currently `tests/playwright`), Testmo `--source` (`frontend-playwright`), variable group (`playwright-variables`), schedule/name rebrands, and **what value should replace the literal `string` placeholder in `ci-manualTestReport.yml`'s env `values` list**. Leave `dockerContainer` alone — the Husky pre-commit hook auto-syncs it to `@playwright/test` and pnpm's major version. If they're on different/no CI, ask whether to remove the Azure files.
7. **Examples & docs** — ask whether to keep the example page objects/specs/screenshots as reference scaffolding or strip them (keep `BasePage` + fixture wiring regardless). Regenerate `README.me` and `AGENTS.md` for the client; the boilerplate README is long and partly garbled, so write a fresh concise one rather than patching it. When writing AGENTS.md, document that `dockerContainer` in `ci-templates/playwrightTemplate.yml` is managed automatically by the Husky pre-commit hook and should not be set manually — do not hardcode a specific image tag. Fix the stale references (`types/pages.ts` → `types/types.ts`; `config/environments/` → `config/`) in `README.me`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.

## When done

1. Run `pnpm lint:fix` and `pnpm typecheck`; fix anything they surface (a missing env file, a dropped key still referenced by a kept spec). If either command surfaces an error you cannot resolve automatically, stop, show the full error output to the user, and ask for guidance before proceeding.
2. Grep for the placeholder tokens — `your-url-here`, `example.com`, `playwright-boilerplate`, `frontend-playwright`, `OptanonAlertBoxClosed`, the collected `ci-manualTestReport.yml` replacement value (verify it was applied), and (if auth is kept) `change-me` and the `← TODO` markers in `objects/pages/LoginPage.ts` — and confirm only intentional matches remain.
3. Summarise: what changed, which envs are wired, what was deleted, and the follow-ups I own (CI secrets, auth credentials + `loginPage` locators if auth was kept, capturing visual baselines with `--update-snapshots`, requesting `data-testid`s).
4. Offer the **`cleanup-boilerplate`** skill (`.github/skills/cleanup-boilerplate/SKILL.md`) as a follow-up pass — it sweeps for anything now unused (leftover example specs/POMs, orphaned `EnvConfig` keys, unused dependencies) and syncs the docs to match. Run it now if the user wants it done in the same session, or point them to it for later.

## Guardrails

- **Confirm before destructive steps** — deleting example specs/screenshots or CI files needs an explicit yes.
- **Don't invent values.** If you don't know a base URL, consent provider, or Testmo project, ask — a leftover placeholder is worse than a question.
- **Don't touch git remotes or push.** Wiring a new remote is my job.
- **Out of scope:** the per-directory `README.me` stubs (`config/`, `objects/`, `types/`, `testFixtures/`) — leave them.
- If the repo is already onboarded (no placeholders left), say so and offer to update specific values instead of re-running the whole wizard.
